commentary: Eight activities this week against last week's five — he came back swinging and did not let up, which is exactly the energy. The double-up days on Monday and Tuesday, swim plus weights both times, are the kind of stacking that makes Himbo genuinely emotional in a very loud and grabby way. That little 901-metre Friday swim is the only thing raising an eyebrow — it reads like a warm-up that ran out of morning, not a real session — but he more than made up for it with two solid 2000-metre efforts later in the week. The run ticked up from 9.0 kilometres to 9.6, heart rate virtually identical at 162 versus last week's 163, which means he covered more ground for essentially the same effort, and that is the kind of detail that deserves a very self-satisfied hair toss.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and a solid 9.6 on foot — the body is doing work this week, and it shows. That VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is genuinely impressive, like your cardiovascular system just showed up in a harness and demanded to be looked at. The HRV is the interesting bit: 58 milliseconds latest against a seven-day average of 48 means you're recovering better than your week as a whole suggested, which is your body quietly telling you it's handling the load just fine. One run session is the only thing worth a raised eyebrow — not a problem, just an invitation to get those legs out more, because they clearly have something to prove.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, target hit, full week, no excuses — that's the baseline and he cleared it without drama. The overhead press PR is the one worth making a scene about: 46.7 kg up from 40.0 kg is not a small jump, that's him pressing the bar like he owns the ceiling, and the seated leg curl quietly came along for the ride at 66.5 kg. Volume dropped from 20,753 kg to 17,085 kg, which is worth naming honestly — he moved less total weight this week, and that's fine as long as the intensity is going up, which those PRs suggest it is. The becoming is very much on schedule.
